examples.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Involving Cosine with Non-Special Angles
examples.problem: Calculate, in radians to $1$ decimal place, the solutions to the equation $\cos x = \dfrac{4}{5}$ for $0 \leq x <   2\pi.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{4}{5})=0.643\,501…≈0.644\end{aligned}
$$

Since $0.644$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is $x_1 = 0.644.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of $\theta_R = 0.644.$ Since $\cos{x} > 0,$ the second solution must lie in the fourth quadrant, and it also has a reference angle $\theta_R = 0.644.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13952163/assets/8ec2e836cb0db78f0811bf8256ec1ab08323b9f3adfe9bd127a8911ece7ee3bd.png)

Since the second solution $x_2$ lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =2\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =2\pi -0.644 \\  & =5.639\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions (rounded to one decimal place) are $x = 0.6, 5.6.$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{cos}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4 & =1 \\ 6\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-3 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{1}{2})=\frac{2\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\frac{2\pi }{3}$ lies inside the specified domain, our first solution is $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}.$

Our first solution lies in the second quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{3}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{3}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13952163/assets/d188a8634c7d33813260472c8691dccdbedbc809d3b59445afc912a43a09675b.png)

Since the second solution $x$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{4\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions of the equation, arranged in ascending order, are $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}$ and $x=\frac{4\pi }{3}.$
